peaks.title_en: One to five spots at five colours
peaks.caption_en: A single projected light pattern sends each colour of the light the chip generates to its own set of spots: one spot at 760 nm, two at 770 nm, three at 780.5 nm, four at 791.5 nm and five at 803 nm. The pattern is the sum of 15 gratings with periods from 16.4 to 16.95 µm, each focusing one colour onto one spot.

facts.periods: 16.4, 16.5375, 16.675, 16.8125, 16.95 µm, one per colour band (SI S11; data r0_list)
facts.spots_per_band: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 spots at 760, 770, 780.5, 791.5, 803 nm (counted in the measured slices; paper: one to five peaks at five wavelengths)
facts.base_patterns: 15 focusing (quadratically chirped) gratings, n_comb,k = k (SI S11, Eq. S89, Fig. S39)
facts.max_gray: 0.8, the maximum grayscale of the illumination (SI S11; data scale)
facts.pump: 60 fs pulses, 100 MHz repetition rate, 40 mW average power on chip (Fig. 5 caption)
facts.bias: 600 V (Fig. 5 caption and SI S11; data Vpp = 6.0, × 100)
facts.unit: SH intensity in nW per µm of transverse position per nm of wavelength, as on the paper's axes
facts.power_scale: camera counts converted to power with a reference image of 11.6 µW total SH power (notebook; calibration image 13, single grating period 16.725 µm)
facts.imaging: x = (camera row − 550) × 3.45 µm / 5.5; SH wavelength = 815.2 − 0.0431 × camera column nm (notebook)
facts.slices: mean over ±0.5 nm around 760, 770, 780.5, 791.5, 803 nm (notebook; dashed lines in the paper's top-right inset)
facts.peak_value: 0.265 nW µm⁻¹ nm⁻¹ (highest pixel; computed from data)

peaks.in_paper_en: Nature 649, 330 (2026), Fig. 5b. 60 fs, 100 MHz pump pulses; 40 mW on chip; bias 600 V.

airy2.title_en: Opposite Airy beams at two colours
airy2.caption_en: Two gratings with periods of 16.4 and 16.95 µm and opposite cubic bends shape the light into two Airy beams, each a bright spot followed by a trail of fringes: at 762 nm the fringes trail off to one side, at 797 nm to the other.

facts.airy_chirps: c_Airy = 1.85 × 10⁻⁵ and −1.32 × 10⁻⁵ rad µm⁻³ (SI S11, Eq. S90)
facts.segments: grating 1 (16.4 µm) on z = 1886–3017.6 µm (SLM columns 500–799); grating 2 (16.95 µm) on z = 3017.6–4149.2 µm (SLM columns 800–1099) (data; SI S11 gives 1886–3019 and 3019–3772 µm)
facts.main_lobes: x = -20.7 µm at 762 nm (fringes towards −x), x = 20.7 µm at 797 nm (fringes towards +x) (computed from the measured slices)
facts.pump: 60 fs pulses, 100 MHz repetition rate, 40 mW average power on chip (Fig. 5 caption)
facts.bias: 600 V (Fig. 5 caption and SI S11; data Vpp = 6.0, × 100)
facts.unit: SH intensity in nW per µm of transverse position per nm of wavelength, as on the paper's axes
facts.power_scale: camera counts converted to power with a reference image of 11.6 µW total SH power (notebook; calibration image 13, single grating period 16.725 µm)
facts.imaging: x = (camera row − 550) × 3.45 µm / 5.5; SH wavelength = 815.2 − 0.0431 × camera column nm (notebook)
facts.slices: mean over ±0.5 nm around 762, 797 nm (notebook; dashed lines in the paper's top-right inset)
facts.peak_value: 0.406 nW µm⁻¹ nm⁻¹ (highest pixel; computed from data)

airy2.in_paper_en: Nature 649, 330 (2026), Fig. 5c. 60 fs, 100 MHz pump pulses; 40 mW on chip; bias 600 V.

grid.title_en: Four spots at each of four colours
grid.caption_en: Another projected pattern puts four spots at each of four colours (760, 773, 787 and 804 nm): a 4 × 4 grid of 16 spots in position and wavelength. It is the sum of 16 focusing gratings, four periods from 16.4 to 16.95 µm, each aimed at the same four positions.

facts.periods: 16.4, 16.5833, 16.7667, 16.95 µm (data r0_list; the SI Fig. S40 caption lists the last one as 16.4 µm, evidently a typo for 16.95)
facts.weights: 0.3, 0.15, 0.12, 0.47 (SI Fig. S40 caption, c1–c4; data amps)
facts.spots_per_band: 4, 4, 4, 4 spots at 760, 773, 787, 804 nm (counted in the measured slices; SI: sixteen distinct peaks)
facts.pump: 60 fs pulses, 100 MHz repetition rate, 40 mW average power on chip as stated for Fig. 5 (Fig. 5 caption); not restated for Fig. S40, which used the same set-up (SI S11)
facts.bias: 600 V (SI S11, for all experiments in that section; data Vpp = 6.0, × 100)
facts.unit: SH intensity in nW per µm of transverse position per nm of wavelength, as on the paper's axes
facts.power_scale: camera counts converted to power with a reference image of 11.6 µW total SH power (notebook; calibration image 13, single grating period 16.725 µm)
facts.imaging: x = (camera row − 550) × 3.45 µm / 5.5; SH wavelength = 815.2 − 0.0431 × camera column nm (notebook)
facts.slices: mean over ±0.5 nm around 760, 773, 787, 804 nm (notebook; dashed lines in the paper's top-right inset)

notes.map: rows = x_um (row 0 = most negative x: draw it at the bottom), cols = lam_nm (increasing); 4 x 4 block means of the notebook's array; colour scale 0..vmax_paper as in the paper (vmax_paper = highest full-resolution pixel)
notes.slices: k x len(x_um): mean over lam in [c - 0.5, c + 0.5] nm for c in slices_nm, block-averaged onto x_um; slices_hires = the same at full camera resolution (the paper's curves exactly). The paper draws the dashed lines at slices_mean_nm and plots slice[i] + i * slice_offset horizontally against x
notes.zoom: projected grayscale (0..1 absolute, Greens, as the paper); row 0 = most negative x; one cell = one SLM pixel = 3.772 um square; draw over extent_*, crop to view_*
notes.chip: pattern at ds_indices (every 17 um along z) over SLM rows y_c +- 120 (every 2nd row), divided by max_gray; row 0 = most negative x
notes.parts: peaks only: the 15 base patterns of SI Fig. S39 in the zoom window, stacked vertically (parts_cell = rows, cols of one cell), order and targets in parts_meta
